office_does: One of two Washington State Representatives for the 41st District (Mercer Island, Newcastle and parts of Bellevue, Issaquah, Renton and Sammamish), voting on state law, budgets and taxes for two-year terms.
race_blurb: House Deputy Majority Leader My-Linh Thai, in office since 2019, faces Independent Michael Rosen, a Mercer Island attorney running on fiscal discipline and refusing special-interest money. Thai took 66% in the August primary.

candidates.summary: Incumbent since 2019 and House Deputy Majority Leader; a pharmacist and former Bellevue School Board president focused on healthcare access, behavioral health, climate and civil rights.
highlights: Voted for the 2026 tax on household income over $1 million (ESSB 6346), which I-645 would repeal [S8]
Voted for 2025 rent stabilization (EHB 1217) and the 2026 supportive-housing siting law (ESHB 2266) [S9][S10]
Top priorities: affordable care, behavioral health and 'meaningful action on climate change' [S1]
Voted for ESHB 1296 (2025); no public position found on the three initiatives [S7]

taxes.basis: Voted yea on ESSB 6346; also cites expanding tax credits and eliminating sales tax on essentials.

spending.basis: Cites securing local project funding and expanding behavioral health, housing and shelter funding.

housing.basis: Voted for rent stabilization and ESHB 2266; cites securing housing and shelter funding.

climate.basis: Lists climate action as a top priority; endorsed by Sierra Club and Washington Conservation Action.

experience.basis: In the House since 2019, now Deputy Majority Leader with eight committee assignments.

local-control.basis: Voted for ESHB 2266, a state requirement that cities allow supportive housing and shelters in specified zones.

immigration.basis: Says she has 'fought to defend immigrant families and workers'; endorsed by CAIR Action.

healthcare.basis: Frames healthcare as 'protecting access to affordable and high-quality care' within the current system; no single-payer statement.

social.basis: Endorsed by WA Planned Parenthood Alliance Advocates and WA Stonewall Democrats; no direct statement on these policies.

parental-rights.basis: Voted yea on ESHB 1296 (2025), which amended the I-2081 parents' rights law; single vote.

candidates.summary: Independent challenger, a Mercer Island attorney, investor and licensed nutritionist without prior elected office, running on fiscal discipline and refusing special-interest money.
highlights: 'Olympia keeps spending more and delivering less'; says state spending 'more than doubled in two decades' [S1]
Calls for 'real fiscal discipline — demanding results from every dollar we spend before asking taxpayers for more' [S3]
'I take no money from special interests'; says he is bound to neither party [S3]
No public position found on the three initiatives [S1][S3]

taxes.basis: Criticizes rising taxes and Olympia 'asking families for more'; no position on specific taxes.

spending.basis: Fiscal discipline is the core of both his pamphlet statement and his general-election profile.

safety.basis: Says people with addiction or mental illness need 'real treatment and recovery, not simply a roof without adequate support': indirect skepticism of housing-first.

experience.basis: No elected experience; first run for office as an independent.

reform.basis: Says he takes no money from special interests and is bound to neither party.
